title: The LP2 grid’s 4-prefix cells
question: Do the seventeen 4-prefix cells supply evidence for a separate nibble channel?
summary: The restricted suffix range follows exactly from byte-sized base 60. The cells are positionally concentrated under two simple placement controls; no readout or key is specified.

scope.representation: The original 32×8 table of case-sensitive two-character tokens; focus only on cells beginning with 4.
scope.procedure: Count suffix symbols; check byte-bounded base-60 maximum; measure four eight-row block counts and orthogonal adjacencies; compare fixed marked-cell placement controls.
scope.parameters: 17 marked cells; 20,000 seeded global-position and row-count-preserving column trials; no output decoding.
scope.exclusions: Transcription alternatives affecting other cells, adaptive routes, a proposed key and plaintext.

finding: Seventeen cells have 11 distinct suffix symbols; 0–9/A–F are permitted by a one-byte base-60 interpretation, with five hexadecimal symbols absent. Seven touching pairs occur; 43/20,000 global and 464/20,000 row-conditioned placements had at least seven.
limitations: The position measures were chosen after seeing the grid. Neither control models its creation. Restricted suffixes are a byte-range consequence, not evidence for a second layer.
next_steps: Specify a fixed cell order, decoding rule and held-out output before treating the positions as a cipher.

review.reviewer: Independent computational recount against archived text

reproduction.environment: Python 3.12 standard library; independent check: python experiments/records/grid-high-digit-cells/check.py
